items.front: Who founded Vijayanagara, when, and under whose guidance?
items.back: Harihara I & Bukka Raya I (Sangama) in 1336, guided by Saint Vidyaranya.
items.examPoint: Vijayanagara founding 1336 — Harihara I & Bukka Raya I, Sangama brothers, Saint Vidyaranya
Four ruling dynasties & sequence — Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu

items.front: Greatest Vijayanagara ruler, his dynasty and title?
items.back: Krishnadevaraya (Tuluva, r.1509-29), 'Andhra Bhoja'; Babur's Baburnama called him most powerful.
items.examPoint: Krishnadevaraya — zenith of empire, Andhra Bhoja, Baburnama praise, Tuluva dynasty

items.front: Krishnadevaraya's Telugu and Sanskrit literary works?
items.back: Amuktamalyada (Telugu, on polity) and Jambavati Kalyanam (Sanskrit).
items.examPoint: Krishnadevaraya's literary works — Amuktamalyada (Telugu), Jambavati Kalyanam (Sanskrit)

items.front: What were the Ashtadiggajas, and who led them?
items.back: Eight great Telugu court poets of Krishnadevaraya; led by Allasani Peddana (Andhra Kavita Pitamaha).
items.examPoint: Ashtadiggajas — eight Telugu poets & the classic era of Telugu literature

items.front: Capital of Vijayanagara and its famous temples?
items.back: Hampi on the Tungabhadra (goddess Pampadevi); Virupaksha & Vittala (musical pillars, stone chariot).
items.examPoint: Vijayanagara architecture — Virupaksha & Vittala temples, musical pillars, stone chariot, Dravidian style

items.front: Battle of Talikota (1565): who lost, and to whom?
items.back: Vijayanagara under regent Aliya Rama Raya lost to a Deccan Sultanate coalition; Hampi was sacked.
items.examPoint: Battle of Talikota 1565 — Aliya Rama Raya, Deccan Sultanate coalition, decline of Vijayanagara

items.back: Nayankara (military chiefs hold land for troops) & ayagars; Mandala > Nadu > Sthala > Grama.
items.examPoint: Vijayanagara administration — Mandala/Nadu/Sthala/Grama, nayankara & ayagar systems

items.front: Match foreign travellers to Vijayanagara with their lands.
items.back: Nicolo de Conti (Italy), Abdur Razzaq (Persia), Domingo Paes & Fernao Nunes (Portugal).
items.examPoint: Foreign travellers to Vijayanagara — Nicolo de Conti, Abdur Razzaq, Domingo Paes, Fernao Nunes

items.front: Who founded the Bahmani kingdom, when, and from what?
items.back: Alauddin Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu) in 1347, by revolting from the Delhi Sultanate.
items.examPoint: Bahmani founding 1347 — Alauddin Bahman Shah (Hasan Gangu), revolt from Delhi Sultanate

items.back: Gulbarga first, then Bidar (shifted by Ahmad Shah Wali).
items.examPoint: Bahmani capitals — Gulbarga then Bidar (shifted by Ahmad Shah Wali)

items.front: Iranian PM who built the Bidar madrasa and was executed in 1482?
items.back: Mahmud Gawan; reformed revenue and expanded the kingdom before nobles' conspiracy killed him.
items.examPoint: Mahmud Gawan — reforms, conquests, Bidar madrasa & execution in 1482

items.front: Five Deccan Sultanates and their dynasties?
items.back: Bijapur (Adil Shahi), Ahmednagar (Nizam Shahi), Golconda (Qutb Shahi), Berar (Imad Shahi), Bidar (Barid Shahi).
items.examPoint: Disintegration into five Deccan Sultanates — Bijapur, Golconda, Ahmednagar, Berar, Bidar (founders & dynasties)

items.front: Gol Gumbaz and Charminar — which dynasties/cities?
items.back: Gol Gumbaz — Adil Shahi (Bijapur, largest dome in Asia); Charminar — Qutb Shahi (Hyderabad).
items.examPoint: Deccan Sultanate architecture — Gol Gumbaz, Charminar, Ibrahim Roza

items.front: What was the flashpoint of the Vijayanagara-Bahmani rivalry?
items.back: The Raichur Doab (between Krishna & Tungabhadra); fuelled by horse trade via the Portuguese.
items.examPoint: Vijayanagara-Bahmani rivalry — Krishna-Tungabhadra (Raichur) doab, horse trade, Portuguese
